atoms.text: This guide configures the EdgeRoute load balancer to deliver access logs into an object storage bucket named lb-access-logs in the same account as the load balancer. EdgeRoute writes one gzip-compressed log object every five minutes under the prefix lb/prod/. Create an IAM role named EdgeRouteLogWriter in account 111111111111 and set its trust policy to allow the EdgeRoute delivery service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows the storage:PutObject action on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs/lb/prod/*. The bucket and the role are in the same account, so this identity-based policy alone grants the access. Do not modify the bucket policy. In the EdgeRoute console, enable access logging, select lb-access-logs as the destination, enter lb/prod/ as the prefix, and choose EdgeRouteLogWriter as the delivery role. After saving, wait one delivery interval and list the prefix to confirm that the first .gz object exists. If no object appears, check the role's trust relationship and confirm that the resource ARN in the policy matches the bucket name and prefix exactly.

This guide configures the EdgeRoute load balancer to deliver access logs into an object storage bucket named lb-access-logs, which is owned by a different account than the load balancer. EdgeRoute writes one gzip-compressed log object every five minutes under the prefix lb/prod/. The load balancer's account, 111111111111, contains an IAM role named EdgeRouteLogWriter whose trust policy allows the EdgeRoute delivery service to assume it. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds a statement to the bucket policy that names arn:example:iam::111111111111:role/EdgeRouteLogWriter as the principal and allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs/lb/prod/*. Because the bucket is in another account, this bucket policy statement carries the grant. In the EdgeRoute console of account 111111111111, enable access logging, select lb-access-logs as the destination, enter lb/prod/ as the prefix, and choose EdgeRouteLogWriter as the delivery role. After saving, wait one delivery interval and have the bucket owner list the prefix to confirm that the first .gz object exists. If no object appears, check the principal ARN in the bucket policy and confirm that the resource ARN matches the bucket name and prefix exactly. The bucket owner should also confirm that the statement is not overridden by an explicit deny.

This guide sets up delivery of audit trail events from the AuditStream service to a bucket named audit-trail-archive in the same account. AuditStream writes JSON event files, batched every ten minutes, under the prefix events/. Create an IAM role named AuditStreamDelivery in account 111111111111 and allow the AuditStream service to assume it through the trust policy. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::audit-trail-archive/events/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on the bucket itself. The role and the bucket share an account, so the identity-based policy is the only grant required. Leave the bucket policy unchanged. In the AuditStream settings, create a trail, set audit-trail-archive as the destination, set events/ as the prefix, and select AuditStreamDelivery as the role. Save the trail and start logging. Within about fifteen minutes, list the events/ prefix and confirm that at least one JSON file has been written. A missing file usually means the policy's resource ARN does not include the events/ prefix.

This guide sets up delivery of audit trail events from the AuditStream service to a bucket named audit-trail-archive, which belongs to a different account than the trail. AuditStream writes JSON event files, batched every ten minutes, under the prefix events/. The trail's account, 111111111111, holds an IAM role named AuditStreamDelivery, which the AuditStream service assumes through its trust policy. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds a bucket policy statement with arn:example:iam::111111111111:role/AuditStreamDelivery as the principal. The statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::audit-trail-archive/events/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on the bucket itself. The bucket policy therefore carries the grant across the account boundary. In the AuditStream settings of account 111111111111, create a trail, set audit-trail-archive as the destination, set events/ as the prefix, and select AuditStreamDelivery as the role. Save the trail and start logging. Within about fifteen minutes, the bucket owner should list the events/ prefix and confirm that at least one JSON file has been written. A missing file usually means the bucket policy's resource ARN does not include the events/ prefix.

This guide covers delivery of network flow records from the NetFlowLens service into a bucket named vpc-flow-records in a single account. NetFlowLens writes one compressed file per capture interval, partitioned by date as year/month/day/ under the prefix flows/. Create an IAM role named NetFlowLensWriter in account 111111111111, with a trust policy that names the NetFlowLens service as the entity allowed to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::vpc-flow-records/flows/*. Since the role and bucket are in the same account, no bucket policy statement is needed, and the existing bucket policy must stay as it is. In NetFlowLens, create a flow capture for the target network, choose vpc-flow-records as the destination, and set the prefix to flows/. Select NetFlowLensWriter as the delivery role and set the capture interval to ten minutes. After the first interval, list flows/ and verify that a date-partitioned directory with a compressed file inside exists. Downstream query tools in the same account will read this layout without further changes.

This guide covers delivery of network flow records from the NetFlowLens service into a bucket named vpc-flow-records, which is owned by a different account than the monitored network. NetFlowLens writes one compressed file per capture interval, partitioned by date as year/month/day/ under the prefix flows/. The monitored network's account, 111111111111, contains an IAM role named NetFlowLensWriter, with a trust policy that names the NetFlowLens service as the entity allowed to assume it. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:example:iam::111111111111:role/NetFlowLensWriter as the principal and allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::vpc-flow-records/flows/*. The grant lives in the bucket policy, because the bucket is in another account. In NetFlowLens, create a flow capture for the target network, choose vpc-flow-records as the destination, and set the prefix to flows/. Select NetFlowLensWriter as the delivery role and set the capture interval to ten minutes. After the first interval, the bucket owner should list flows/ and verify that a date-partitioned directory with a compressed file inside exists. Downstream query tools in the owner's account will read this layout without further changes.

This guide configures the EdgeCache content delivery service to write request logs into a bucket named cdn-request-logs in the same account. EdgeCache produces one gzip file per distribution every hour, named with the distribution ID and a timestamp, under the prefix cdn/. Create an IAM role named EdgeCacheLogRole in account 111111111111 and set its trust policy to permit the EdgeCache logging component to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cdn-request-logs/cdn/* and storage:ListBucket on arn:example:storage:::cdn-request-logs. The role and the bucket are in the same account, so the role's policy grants everything the delivery needs. Do not edit the bucket policy. In the EdgeCache distribution settings, turn on request logging, enter cdn-request-logs as the bucket, cdn/ as the prefix, and EdgeCacheLogRole as the role. Disable cookie logging if the logs should omit cookie headers. After the first hourly run, list the cdn/ prefix and check that an object named with the distribution ID is present.

This guide configures the EdgeCache content delivery service to write request logs into a bucket named cdn-request-logs, which is owned by a different account than the distribution. EdgeCache produces one gzip file per distribution every hour, named with the distribution ID and a timestamp, under the prefix cdn/. The distribution's account, 111111111111, holds an IAM role named EdgeCacheLogRole, and its trust policy permits the EdgeCache logging component to assume it. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:example:iam::111111111111:role/EdgeCacheLogRole as the principal. The statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cdn-request-logs/cdn/* and storage:ListBucket on arn:example:storage:::cdn-request-logs. That bucket policy statement, not an identity-based policy, is what grants the delivery. In the EdgeCache distribution settings, turn on request logging, enter cdn-request-logs as the bucket, cdn/ as the prefix, and EdgeCacheLogRole as the role. Disable cookie logging if the logs should omit cookie headers. After the first hourly run, the bucket owner should list the cdn/ prefix and check that an object named with the distribution ID is present.

This guide exports slow query logs from the QueryTrace database service to a bucket named db-slowlog-export in the same account. QueryTrace writes a text file every thirty minutes containing statements that exceeded the configured duration threshold, under the prefix slowlog/. Create an IAM role named QueryTraceExporter in account 111111111111, and allow the QueryTrace export worker to assume it in the trust policy. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:example:storage:::db-slowlog-export/slowlog/*. As the role and bucket share an account, this policy is the sole source of the grant and the bucket policy is left untouched. In the QueryTrace instance settings, set the slow query threshold to 2000 milliseconds, enable log export, and enter db-slowlog-export as the destination with slowlog/ as the prefix. Select QueryTraceExporter as the export role and apply the change without restarting the instance. After thirty minutes, list slowlog/ and confirm that a text file is present. Large files are uploaded in multiple parts, which is why the abort permission is included.

This guide exports slow query logs from the QueryTrace database service to a bucket named db-slowlog-export, which is owned by a different account than the database instance. QueryTrace writes a text file every thirty minutes containing statements that exceeded the configured duration threshold, under the prefix slowlog/. The instance's account, 111111111111, contains an IAM role named QueryTraceExporter, which the QueryTrace export worker may assume through its trust policy. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:example:iam::111111111111:role/QueryTraceExporter as the principal. The statement allows storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:example:storage:::db-slowlog-export/slowlog/*, and it is the sole source of the grant. In the QueryTrace instance settings, set the slow query threshold to 2000 milliseconds, enable log export, and enter db-slowlog-export as the destination with slowlog/ as the prefix. Select QueryTraceExporter as the export role and apply the change without restarting the instance. After thirty minutes, the bucket owner should list slowlog/ and confirm that a text file is present. Large files are uploaded in multiple parts, which is why the abort permission is included.

This guide delivers function execution logs from the RunLog serverless runtime to a bucket named fn-exec-logs in the same account. RunLog buffers log lines per function and flushes a newline-delimited JSON object every five minutes or at 5 MB, whichever comes first, under the prefix functions/. Create an IAM role named RunLogShipper in account 111111111111, with a trust policy that lets the RunLog runtime assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::fn-exec-logs/functions/*. Since both resources are in one account, the identity-based policy grants the access and the bucket policy does not change. In the RunLog configuration for each function, set the log sink type to object storage, enter fn-exec-logs as the bucket, and set functions/ as the prefix. Choose RunLogShipper as the shipping role and set the log level to INFO. Invoke the function once, wait for the flush, and list functions/ to confirm that an object named with the function name exists. If the object does not appear, verify that the role is selected on every function that should ship logs.

This guide delivers function execution logs from the RunLog serverless runtime to a bucket named fn-exec-logs, which is owned by a different account than the functions. RunLog buffers log lines per function and flushes a newline-delimited JSON object every five minutes or at 5 MB, whichever comes first, under the prefix functions/. The functions' account, 111111111111, contains an IAM role named RunLogShipper, and its trust policy lets the RunLog runtime assume it. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:example:iam::111111111111:role/RunLogShipper as the principal and allowing storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::fn-exec-logs/functions/*. Since the resources are in separate accounts, the bucket policy statement grants the access. In the RunLog configuration for each function, set the log sink type to object storage, enter fn-exec-logs as the bucket, and set functions/ as the prefix. Choose RunLogShipper as the shipping role and set the log level to INFO. Invoke the function once, wait for the flush, and have the bucket owner list functions/ to confirm that an object named with the function name exists. If the object does not appear, verify that the role is selected on every function that should ship logs.

This guide enables DNS query logging in the ResolverLog service and delivers the records to a bucket named dns-query-logs in the same account. ResolverLog writes a compressed CSV file every fifteen minutes, with one row per query, under the prefix resolver/. Create an IAM role named ResolverLogDelivery in account 111111111111 and allow the ResolverLog service to assume it in the trust policy. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs/resolver/* and storage:GetBucketAcl on the bucket. The role and bucket are in the same account, so this policy alone permits delivery, and no change is made to the bucket policy. In the ResolverLog console, create a query log configuration, associate it with the private zone to be logged, and set dns-query-logs as the destination with resolver/ as the prefix. Select ResolverLogDelivery as the role and save the configuration. After the first fifteen-minute interval, list resolver/ and open one file to confirm that the columns include timestamp, query name, record type, and response code. If the console reports a destination validation error, review the GetBucketAcl permission, since ResolverLog performs this check during setup.

This guide enables DNS query logging in the ResolverLog service and delivers the records to a bucket named dns-query-logs, which is owned by a different account than the logged zone. ResolverLog writes a compressed CSV file every fifteen minutes, with one row per query, under the prefix resolver/. The zone's account, 111111111111, holds an IAM role named ResolverLogDelivery, and the ResolverLog service may assume it through the trust policy. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds a bucket policy statement with arn:example:iam::111111111111:role/ResolverLogDelivery as the principal. The statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs/resolver/* and storage:GetBucketAcl on the bucket, and this statement alone permits delivery across the account boundary. In the ResolverLog console of account 111111111111, create a query log configuration, associate it with the private zone to be logged, and set dns-query-logs as the destination with resolver/ as the prefix. Select ResolverLogDelivery as the role and save the configuration. After the first fifteen-minute interval, the bucket owner should list resolver/ and open one file to confirm that the columns include timestamp, query name, record type, and response code. If the console reports a destination validation error, review the GetBucketAcl permission in the bucket policy, since ResolverLog performs this check during setup.

This guide configures the GuardPoint firewall to deliver rule-match logs to a bucket named fw-match-logs and lets a compaction job read and rewrite them, all within one account. GuardPoint writes small JSON files every two minutes under the prefix raw/. A compaction job running as the IAM role GuardPointCompactor in account 111111111111 reads the raw/ objects hourly and writes merged files under the prefix compacted/. Create the delivery role GuardPointWriter with a trust policy for the GuardPoint service and an identity-based policy allowing storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::fw-match-logs/raw/*. Give GuardPointCompactor an identity-based policy allowing storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on the bucket and raw/*, plus storage:PutObject on compacted/*. Because everything is in the same account, these identity-based policies provide all access, and the bucket policy is not modified. In GuardPoint, set the log destination to fw-match-logs with the raw/ prefix and choose GuardPointWriter as the role. Run the compaction job once and verify that a merged file appears under compacted/. The merged file should contain every record from the raw/ objects processed in that run.

This guide configures the GuardPoint firewall to deliver rule-match logs to a bucket named fw-match-logs and lets a compaction job read and rewrite them, with the bucket owned by a different account than the firewall and the job. GuardPoint writes small JSON files every two minutes under the prefix raw/. A compaction job running as the IAM role GuardPointCompactor in account 111111111111 reads the raw/ objects hourly and writes merged files under the prefix compacted/. The delivery role GuardPointWriter, also in account 111111111111, has a trust policy for the GuardPoint service. The bucket owner, account 222222222222, adds bucket policy statements naming both role ARNs as principals. One allows storage:PutObject on raw/* for GuardPointWriter, and the other allows storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on the bucket and raw/*, plus storage:PutObject on compacted/*, for GuardPointCompactor. The bucket policy carries all access because the bucket is in another account. In GuardPoint, set the log destination to fw-match-logs with the raw/ prefix and choose GuardPointWriter as the role. Run the compaction job once and have the bucket owner verify that a merged file appears under compacted/. The merged file should contain every record from the raw/ objects processed in that run.
